# Balloon Lettering

## Purpose

Get the words onto the page so they are read in the right order, by the right
speaker, without covering what the panel is about. Lettering has two halves.
The text is fixed in `page.yaml` and never drifts from it. The placement is
planned per panel and then either drawn by the image model (`in_image`) or set
on top of the finished art (`overlay`).

## Use When

- `/lettering` plans, places, or checks the text of a page.
- A panel script has dialogue and nobody has decided where it sits.
- A render came back with misspelled, missing, or misattributed text.
- The project switches between `in_image` and `overlay` lettering.

## Inputs

- The `lettering` list of every panel in
  `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/page.yaml`: `id`, `type`,
  `speaker`, `text`, `order`.
- `production/project.yaml`: `language`, `reading_direction`, and the
  `lettering` block (`mode`, `font_family`, `case`, `max_words_per_balloon`,
  `max_words_per_panel`), plus `page.safe_margin_mm`.
- `production/style/style-bible.md` for the lettering style.
- The provider's `textRendering` capability in
  `manifests/image-providers.json`.
- Overlay mode: the render the overlay sits on, and the page's
  `lettering.yaml` if one exists.

## Process

1. Fix the words. Each entry's `text` holds the exact approved string, with
   every accent and punctuation mark of the project's `language`. Store the
   words in their normal capitalization. `lettering.case` decides how they
   are drawn, and upper case keeps its accents and opening marks. Any change
   of wording goes through the writer and lands in `page.yaml` first.
2. Give each entry the right `type`: `caption` for a box of place or time,
   `narration` for the narrator's voice, `balloon` for normal speech,
   `thought`, `whisper`, `shout`, `radio` for a voice through a device, `sfx`
   for a sound, and `sign` for text that exists inside the world (a painted
   hull name, a notice). Spoken types carry a `speaker` who is in the panel's
   `cast`. A voice from outside the frame needs an off-panel row for its
   speaker.
3. Check the word budgets. Count the words per balloon and per panel against
   `max_words_per_balloon` and `max_words_per_panel`. When a balloon runs
   over, split it into two entries with consecutive `order` values, move a
   line to another panel, or ask the writer to cut. Shrinking the type to
   fit is not an option.
4. Set the reading order. `order` values are unique within the page and rise
   along the panel reading order. Inside a panel the reader starts at the
   top corner where the reading path enters (top left in `ltr`, top right in
   `rtl`) and moves across and down. The first line spoken sits highest and
   nearest that corner. If the second speaker stands on the entry side, ask
   `panel-composition` to restage. Crossed tails are not a fix.
5. Place each element so it hides nothing the panel needs. Keep balloons off
   faces, off hands, off any prop that is held or changes custody, and off
   the contact point of an action. Use the quiet area the composition
   reserved. Stay inside the safe margin, and keep a balloon clearly inside
   its own panel unless the overlap is a planned device.
6. Point every tail at its speaker. The tail aims at the mouth and stops
   short of the face. For an off-panel speaker it points to the panel edge on
   the side where that character stands in the ledger. Captions, narration,
   signs, and sound effects have no tail.
7. Treat sound effects as drawing. A sound effect is part of the art: its
   size states the volume, its position marks the source, and its shape
   follows the motion that made it. Keep each one short, place it at the
   thing that makes the noise, and do not put it in a balloon.
8. Choose the mode from `lettering.mode`. No provider declares
   `textRendering: reliable`, so use `in_image` only when the user accepts
   repair cycles for text, and never with a provider whose value is `none`
   (comfyui): the compiler refuses it. Otherwise use `overlay`.
9. `in_image`: the page prompt carries every string with its panel, type,
   speaker, and reading order, and asks for balloons clear of faces, hands,
   and the action. It carries no coordinates, so reserve the room a balloon
   needs in the panel's `framing.composition`. The prompt package lists the
   strings under `lettering_text`. After
   generation, the review's `lettering` check compares each drawn string
   with `page.yaml` letter by letter. A wrong letter is a finding and a
   repair. Nobody retypes text into the image by hand.
10. `overlay`: generate the art with no text and no balloons, then write
    `lettering.yaml` next to `page.yaml` with the `render` it sits on, the
    `canvas` size, the `font`, and one element per lettering entry: `id`,
    `panel`, `type`, `text`, `box` in pixels, `shape`, `tail`, and `style`.
    Default shapes: `rect` for captions and narration, `ellipse` for balloons
    and whispers, `cloud` for thoughts, `burst` for shouts and radio voices,
    `none` for sound effects and signs.
11. Overlay: copy each `text` from `page.yaml` without retyping it. The two
    files must hold identical strings. Then run
    `node scripts/letter-pages.js --page <page.yaml> --render <RENDER_ID>`,
    which writes `renders/<RENDER_ID>.lettered.svg`. Open the SVG over the
    render and check every box against steps 4 to 6. A new render of the
    page needs its boxes checked again, because the figures may have moved.
12. Run the workspace gate and fix every error reported for the page:
    `node scripts/validate-workspace.js --root <workspace> --issue <ISS_ID>`.

## Outputs

- The `lettering` lists in `page.yaml`, with types, speakers, exact text, and
  page-wide `order` (`page.schema.json`).
- Overlay mode: `production/issues/<ISS_ID>/pages/<PG_ID>/lettering.yaml`
  (`lettering.schema.json`) and `renders/<RENDER_ID>.lettered.svg`.
- In-image mode: placement notes per panel for the reviewer, and the room
  each balloon needs written into the panel's `framing.composition`.
- A lettering check per page: strings compared, budgets counted, order
  traced.

## Quality Bar

- Every string on the page equals its `text` in `page.yaml`, accents
  included.
- In overlay mode, every element's `text` in `lettering.yaml` equals the
  entry with the same `id` in `page.yaml`, and no entry is missing.
- `order` values are unique within the page and follow the panel reading
  order.
- No balloon exceeds `max_words_per_balloon` and no panel exceeds
  `max_words_per_panel`.
- Every spoken element has a speaker in the panel's `cast` and a tail that
  reaches toward that character.
- No element covers a face, a hand, a held prop, or the point of contact.

## Common Failure Modes

- An accent dropped or a word swapped by the image model, and the page
  passed because the caption "was about right".
- A tail pointing at the wrong person, which reassigns the line and can make
  the wrong character seem to act.
- The reply placed above the question because the second speaker stands on
  the entry side.
- Text over the hand that holds the weapon, hiding the one thing the panel
  shows.
- Forty words in a `small` panel, set in type too small to read.
- Narration missing from the render and nobody counted the strings.
- `lettering.yaml` edited to fix a typo while `page.yaml` keeps the old
  word, so the next build brings the typo back.
- A sound effect set in a neat balloon like a spoken line.

## Notes

`letter-pages.js` writes an SVG overlay. It does not flatten the overlay into
a PNG: that step needs a browser or a vector tool, and the flattened file is
what an edition lists as `lettered_file`.

The `lettering` check in a visual review covers exact words, accents,
speaker, tail, reading order, and placement. This skill plans all of those
before generation and checks them again after it. Dialogue length is a
writing decision: when the budget does not fit, the answer comes from
`comic-scripting`, and the letterer does not trim lines alone.
